prompt: Why does the planner's server listen on `127.0.0.1` and not on every address?
hint: It has no password and accepts anything posted to it.

choices.text: Python cannot listen on any other address
choices.why: `ThreadingHTTPServer` takes any address; this one was chosen.

choices.text: So that nothing else on the network reaches it
choices.why: Right: `127.0.0.1` means this machine, which suits a server with no password.

choices.text: Because App Transport Security requires that address
choices.why: ATS is about the app's connections, and since iOS 17 it refuses IP addresses by default.

choices.text: To make the responses arrive faster than over Wi-Fi
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; who can reach it is.

prompt: Match each request to what the planner's server answers.
hint: Section 02 tried three of them with `curl`.

prompt: You stop the server with `Ctrl-C` and start it again. What happened to the session you posted?
hint: Where does the server keep its sessions?

choices.text: It is still there, in a file beside `serve.py`
choices.why: The server writes no file; its lists live in memory.

choices.text: It comes back once the app posts it a second time on start
choices.why: Nothing reposts it; the app has not been written to.

choices.text: It is gone: the lists start again from the four in the file
choices.why: Right, and for a course that is useful: every run starts from the same data.

choices.text: It is kept, marked as done
choices.why: Nothing marks it; it is simply not kept.

prompt: On Linux, `URLSession.shared` gives `type 'URLSession' (aka 'AnyObject') has no member 'shared'`. What is missing?
hint: On Linux the networking types live in a module of their own.

choices.text: `import FoundationNetworking`
choices.why: Right: the open-source Foundation keeps `URLSession` there, behind `#if canImport`.

choices.text: A newer Swift toolchain than 6.4.2
choices.why: 6.4.2 has `URLSession`; the file did not import the module that holds it.

choices.text: `libcurl4-openssl-dev`, from the `apt` line of lesson 1
choices.why: That package was installed; a missing library fails when linking, not with this message.

choices.text: `import SwiftUI`
choices.why: SwiftUI does not exist on Linux, and it is not where `URLSession` lives.

prompt: `URLSession.shared.data(from:)` gets a `404` from the server. What does the call do?
hint: To `URLSession`, only a missing answer is an error.

choices.text: Throws a `URLError` with code 404
choices.why: No error is thrown for an HTTP status; `URLError` codes are about the connection.

choices.text: Returns, with the status in the response
choices.why: Right, which is why section 05's client checks the status itself.

choices.text: Returns an empty `Data` and no response
choices.why: The body arrives too: here it was `{"error": …}`.

choices.text: Retries the request until it gets a `200`
choices.why: `URLSession` does not retry a status for you.

prompt: Why does the course prefer SwiftUI's `task` modifier for starting a load from a view?
hint: What happens to the work when the view goes away?

choices.text: It runs the request on the main thread, which is faster
choices.why: The request runs wherever `URLSession` runs it; speed is not the point.

choices.text: It retries automatically when the network comes back
choices.why: It does no retrying; that is the screen's choice.

choices.text: It cancels the work when the view disappears
choices.why: Right; a `Task` started in `onAppear` is cancelled by nothing.

choices.text: It is the only place `await` is allowed in SwiftUI
choices.why: Any asynchronous context allows `await`, a `Task` included.

prompt: In `WireSession`, the enum that maps `courseID` to the server's `courseId` is called ___.
hint: It conforms to `CodingKey`.

prompt: Which `DecodingError` does a body with `"course_id"` instead of `"courseId"` produce?
hint: The type requires a key the JSON does not have.

choices.text: `typeMismatch`, at the path `course_id`
choices.why: A type mismatch is a value of the wrong type, like `"forty"` for an `Int`.

choices.text: `keyNotFound`, for `courseId`
choices.why: Right: the decoder looked for `courseId` and found no such key.

choices.text: None: the extra key is ignored and `courseID` is empty
choices.why: Extra keys are ignored, but a missing required one throws; nothing is left half-built.

choices.text: `dataCorrupted`, because the JSON is not valid
choices.why: The JSON is valid; it has a different key in it.

prompt: A colleague makes `StudySession` itself `Codable` and drops `WireSession`. The server later sends dates as Unix timestamps. What breaks first?
hint: Where would the model's shape have to change?

choices.text: Nothing: `JSONDecoder` converts a timestamp into the day text
choices.why: A number does not decode into a `String`; it is a `typeMismatch`.

choices.text: Only the tests, which can be updated
choices.why: The decoding fails in the app as well as in the tests.

choices.text: Decoding, and the fix changes the type all screens use
choices.why: Right. With a wire type, the change stays in `Wire.swift` and the model keeps its day.

choices.text: The server, which refuses the old date format on `POST`
choices.why: The question is about the app reading the server's answers.

prompt: After adding `WireTests.swift`, how many tests did `swift test` report in its last line?
hint: Two from lesson 1, two new.

prompt: Put the client's checks in the order `send` makes them.
hint: Answer, status, shape.
items: Was there an answer at all, or was it cancelled?
Does the body decode as the expected type?

prompt: Somebody moves the decoding in `send` above the status check. The server answers `500` with `{"error": "database down"}`. What does the screen get?
hint: Try to decode an error message as a list of courses.

choices.text: `status(500, "database down")`, as before
choices.why: The status is never reached: decoding failed first.

choices.text: `unreadable`: the app blames itself
choices.why: Right: the error page is read as data, and the message says it is a bug in the app.

choices.text: `offline`, so the screen offers a retry
choices.why: There was an answer; offline is for no answer at all.

choices.text: An empty list of courses
choices.why: An object does not decode as an array; it throws rather than producing an empty one.

prompt: What did the client report when nothing was listening on port 8099?
hint: It is one of the `offline` cases.

choices.why: A status needs a server to send it; nothing answered.

choices.text: `offline("timedOut")`
choices.why: A refused connection fails at once; a timeout is section 07's slow server.

choices.text: `unreadable("the body was empty")`
choices.why: Unreadable is a success with the wrong body.

choices.text: `offline("cannotConnectToHost")`
choices.why: Right: the `URLError` code for a refused connection.

prompt: Why is the base URL passed to `APIClient` rather than written inside it?
hint: Think of where the planner runs.

choices.text: One client, this machine or a real server
choices.why: Right, and a test can hand it whatever it needs.

choices.text: Swift does not allow a URL literal inside a struct
choices.why: It does; `fetch` writes URLs inline.

choices.text: `URLSession` refuses a request to a hard-coded address
choices.why: `URLSession` cannot tell where an address came from.

choices.text: App Transport Security reads it from the initializer
choices.why: ATS reads `Info.plist`, never an initializer.

prompt: Why is a screen's load modelled as one `Loadable` enum rather than three properties `isLoading`, `courses` and `error`?
hint: Count the combinations each one allows.

choices.text: An enum uses less memory than three properties
choices.why: Memory is not the argument; impossible states are.

choices.text: One state at a time, each drawn by a `switch`
choices.why: Right: three properties allow loading and an error at once, and nothing insists the error is drawn.

choices.text: SwiftUI can only observe enums, not booleans
choices.why: SwiftUI observes any stored state; lesson 6 uses plain values.

choices.text: `URLSession` returns a `Loadable` directly
choices.why: `Loadable` is the planner's own type, in `Loadable.swift`.

prompt: Which of these errors does the planner offer a retry for? Choose all that apply.
hint: A retry only where asking again could give a different answer.

choices.text: `offline("timedOut")`
choices.why: Yes: the network may come back.

choices.text: `status(500, …)`
choices.why: Yes: a server error can pass.

choices.text: `status(404, …)`
choices.why: No: the course is gone, and asking again gives the same 404.

choices.text: `unreadable(…)`
choices.why: No: the same answer gives the same bug.

prompt: Why is the message for `cancelled` an empty string?
hint: Who started the load, and where are they now?

choices.text: Because the server sends no body when a request is cancelled
choices.why: The message is the app's own sentence, not the server's.

choices.text: It is a placeholder to be translated later
choices.why: It is empty on purpose, and section 06 says why.

choices.text: The screen that asked has gone, so there is nobody to tell
choices.why: Right; section 07's `task(id:)` code writes nothing at all for a cancelled load.

choices.text: Swift does not allow an enum case without a message
choices.why: It does; `cancelled` has no associated value at all.

prompt: The fetch with `?delay=3` was cancelled after 300 ms. What did the server do?
hint: Look at the end of the server's log in section 02.

choices.text: Stopped at once, because the client cancelled
choices.why: The server did not know; it slept its three seconds.

choices.text: Answered later, to a client that had gone
choices.why: Right: cancelling stops the waiting, not work that already reached the server.

choices.text: Logged a `499` status for the request
choices.why: The log says `200` and then that the client had gone.

choices.text: Crashed with a broken pipe
choices.why: `reply` catches the broken pipe and logs one line.

prompt: A request is cancelled before it starts and another is stopped in flight. Which errors reach `send`, and what does it make of them?
hint: Cancelling arrives in two shapes.

choices.text: Both arrive as `URLError(.timedOut)`, which becomes `offline`
choices.why: A timeout is different from a cancellation, and the client keeps them apart.

choices.text: Two errors, both made `.cancelled`
choices.why: Right: two shapes, one meaning for a screen.

choices.text: Neither: a cancelled request returns an empty body
choices.why: A cancelled call throws; it returns no body.

choices.text: A `status(499, "")` from the server for both of them
choices.why: No status comes back for a request nobody waited for.

prompt: How many seconds did the impatient client's session wait for data before giving up?
hint: It is `timeoutIntervalForRequest`.

prompt: In `CourseDetailView`, why does the `task(id:)` code return early when the load came back `.failed(.cancelled)`?
hint: When is it cancelled?

choices.text: To retry the same course once more
choices.why: It does not retry; it leaves the state alone.

choices.text: To keep a spinner on screen until the network returns
choices.why: The new load sets its own state; the old one stays silent.

choices.text: A newer load for another course has replaced it
choices.why: Right: the old load must not land its sessions on top of the new course's.

choices.text: Because `Loadable.run` cannot represent a cancellation
choices.why: It can: `.failed(.cancelled)` is exactly that.

prompt: On iOS 17, which `Info.plist` key lets the planner reach `http://127.0.0.1:8012` during development, and nothing more?
hint: The narrow exception, not the wide one.

choices.text: `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`
choices.why: That turns ATS off for everything and has to be justified to review.

choices.text: `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`
choices.why: Right: local names and IP addresses, which iOS 17 stopped allowing by default.

choices.text: `NSExceptionDomains` with `localhost`
choices.why: The URL uses an IP address, and the narrow local key covers it.

choices.text: No key: ATS ignores port numbers above 8000
choices.why: ATS has no rule about port numbers.

prompt: Why did every `http` request in this lesson work on Linux without any exception?
hint: Where does ATS live?

choices.text: Because Linux encrypts local traffic for you
choices.why: Nothing encrypted it; the server speaks plain HTTP.

choices.text: ATS lives in Apple's systems, not the open Foundation
choices.why: Right, which is also why this section was not run.

choices.text: Because the server sent `Content-Type: application/json`
choices.why: The content type has nothing to do with ATS.

choices.text: Because port 8012 counts as HTTPS
choices.why: The scheme, not the port, says whether it is HTTPS.

prompt: A student on a train opens the planner, and the course list request times out. Trace it: which `APIError`, which `Loadable`, and what does `CourseListView` draw?
hint: Stage one fails; the error can be retried.

choices.text: `status(408, "")`, `.failed`, a message with no button
choices.why: A timeout produces no status; nothing answered.

choices.text: `cancelled`, `.loading`, a spinner that stays
choices.why: Nobody cancelled it; the session gave up waiting.

choices.text: `offline("timedOut")`, `.failed`, the offline message and a Try again button
choices.why: Right: offline can be retried, so the button is drawn.

choices.text: `unreadable(…)`, `.loaded([])`, an empty list
choices.why: No body arrived to be unreadable, and `run` never turns an error into a list.

prompt: Which part of this lesson ran on the Linux machine, and which was only written from Apple's documentation? Pick the one that was NOT run.
hint: SwiftUI is the line.

choices.text: The `fetch` program and its three outcomes
choices.why: That ran: section 05 shows its output.

choices.text: The cancelled and timed-out requests
choices.why: Those ran: section 07 shows them.

choices.text: `CourseListView` drawing the three states
choices.why: Right: it is SwiftUI, written from the documentation and not run.

choices.text: The `WireTests` decoding tests
choices.why: They ran under `swift test` in section 04.
